analysis:
The PR changes documentation only: docs/architecture/inference.md (date bump and a new startup shape-warmup section near lines 956-986 of head, with the supplied units covering only the later, unchanged-looking MiMo/Flint/Flash-Next content) and docs/provider/cli-reference.md (one new env-var row at head line 1751 for DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP). No code, wire protocol, key custody, attestation, authorization or cache-storage behavior changes in the supplied evidence, so no regression against TB-002/TB-003/TB-007/TB-011 or T-041 is identified.

Security-relevant notes for integration: the documented warmup runs synthetic greedy probes at load time and reportedly does not train rates or counters. It runs before registration, so routed consumer traffic should not be affected. It uses synthetic prompts, so it should not touch A-001 or the SSD prefix cache (T-041). I could not verify from the supplied units that warmup prompts bypass cache donation to the encrypted SSD tier or that cache salts are never shared with real traffic. The warmup section's full text (lines ~956-986) is outside my supplied units and only visible as a truncated patch excerpt. The new env var `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP` (0 / always) is an operator-local tuning knob, not a trust-boundary input. It appears to be only a performance or availability control. The row is documented as passed through the shell/environment table, and I did not see evidence that it is a daemon-passthrough variable that weakens a security gate. The cli-reference row sits beside other passthrough keys; whether it is in the LaunchAgent passthrough list was not shown. A reviewer of the code side should confirm the warmup probes cannot donate to the SSD cache, cannot extend the 30-minute TTL oracle (SEC-035), and that the 20 s budget plus preemption cannot delay registration indefinitely (availability). Documentation-only; the threat model need not change on this evidence.
